The figure on this page comes from one line of markdown:

```markdown
![Mean ratings by condition.](ratings.png){#fig-ratings .wrap-right width="40%"}
```

## Result

![Mean ratings by condition.](../images/ratings.png){#fig-ratings .wrap-right width="40%"}

Participants rated each clip on a scale from one to five. @fig-ratings
shows the mean rating in each condition. Ratings in the treatment
condition were higher than ratings in the control condition.

The figure keeps its number and its caption, and this paragraph can point
to it with a `@fig-` link. The class `.wrap-right` puts the figure on the
right side of the text, and the `width` attribute makes it 40% of the
text width.

The paragraphs after the figure flow beside it until the text passes the
bottom of the figure. After that, they run the full width of the text.
Each format
draws the same layout with its own tools: CSS in HTML, wrapfig in LaTeX,
wrap-it in Typst, and a frame in Word.

## Next

A heading is not a paragraph, so wrapping stops before it.
